label: Literal unguarded step2 and its…: Step2 literally says for any proposition p someone knows p…
term: literal unguarded step2 and its common-knower antecedent
definition: Step2 literally says for any proposition p someone knows p, without repeating if-p. The associated step3 antecedent therefore ranges over all propositions, not only truths.
note: This editorial literal reading may conflict with additional factive assumptions, but no such formal system or countermodel is introduced and no equivalence to contextual reading is asserted. The bound body is the literal step2/step3 antecedent ∀ p, ∃ a, knows a p; the common-knower consequent remains a distinct explicit bridge. Content and Agent are arbitrary universe-polymorphic types; truth and actual knowledge are primitive predicates, not a definition of epistemic factivity or modal possibility. Their intended applicability, proposition-domain adequacy and epistemic laws remain open.
